title: Palace: P22.9-B ASEAN budget allocated for the whole year
summary: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday allayed further concerns regarding the P22.9 billion budget allocated for the conduct of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)…

blocks.text: Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Monday allayed further concerns regarding the P22.9 billion budget allocated for the conduct of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summits this year.

Interviewed on Super Radyo dzBB, Castro explained that the P22.9 billion allocation includes expenses for the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu in May, as well as the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila this November.
The Philippines is the chair of ASEAN for 2026.
“‘Yan pa lang po ‘yung allocated budget. It doesn’t mean po na nagastos na po ‘yan. Hindi po,” the Palace Press Officer said.
(That is only the allocated budget. It does not mean that the funds have already been entirely spent.)

“Tandaan po natin, dalawa po ‘yung ginanap diyan---isa sa Cebu, at isa po dito sa Manila. Ang meetings na pinaglaanan niyan ay 550 meetings. Baka isipin ng mga kababayan natin, isang araw lang po ‘yan. Hindi po, buong taon po ‘yan,” she added.

(Remember, two events were held—one in Cebu and another here in Manila. The budget covers a total of 550 meetings. The public might think this budget was just used in just one day, that’s not true. It’s allocated for the whole year.)
Malacañang previously said the government is prepared to audit its spending for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

This, as posts circulated online comparing the government's ASEAN budget of the Marcos administration to the Arroyo and Duterte administrations, which had P1 billion and P3.79 billion, respectively. —AOL, GMA News
